rationale: Both are correct. A finds the root-to-target path and rebuilds only the nodes along it, with good comments, but its index-based loop with i-1/i+1 bookkeeping is somewhat fiddly. The returned tree also shares every off-path subtree with the original by reference, so a change to one tree silently affects the other. B splits the work into small, well-named helper methods (_find, _build_parents, _reorient, _path_to). It treats the tree as an undirected graph: _reorient visits all neighbours, children plus parent, except the one it came from. That is a clean, easy-to-verify formulation, and it produces an entirely fresh tree with no aliasing. Keying the parent map by id() is slightly unusual but sound. B is the cleaner and more robust design.
